review_notes:
I read all 320 lines of the target file. It declares no `@[simp]` lemmas and changes no simp attributes; the only attribute line makes `Classical.propDecidable` a local instance. Its public lemmas are `cubicSymbol_three_periodic`, `cubicSymbol_lambda_periodic`, `cubicSymbol_omega_norm`, `cubicSymbol_omega_periodic`, `cubicSymbol_unit_periodic`, `eisenstein_unit_eq_signed_omega`, `lambdaE_prime` and `cubicSupplementaryPeriodicity_proved`. They are periodicity facts that take `primary`, divisibility or `IsUnit` hypotheses, existential classifications, or a `Prime` fact. None of them makes a sensible simp rewrite: their hypotheses are not ones simp can discharge, and the periodicity equations relate two arbitrary first arguments with no normal-form direction.

I checked how simp is used inside the proofs:
- `simpa only [... normNat_cast]` in `normNat_int`
- `simpa only [← omegaE_primitive.eq_orderOf] using pow_mod_orderOf ...`
- `simpa using omega_cube` (twice)
- `simpa only [hu] using hlam`
- `simpa only [zero_mul, zero_add]`
- `simp` in the `zero` induction case

All of these are local and targeted, with no competing or looping rules.

The closest candidate was the inline `show omega ^ (3 : ℤ) = 1 by simpa using omega_cube`, used in both `cubicSymbol_omega_norm` and `cubicSymbol_omega_periodic`. The same goal is proved by `norm_num [omega_cube]` in CubicThetaCuspCharacter.lean. The upstream lemmas `omega_cube` and `omegaE_cube` (ResidueCharacters.lean) and `lambdaE_sq` (PeriodicPoisson.lean) are not tagged simp. But those declarations live in other files, and the duplication here is only two short occurrences. I did not consider that strong enough to report as a simp-interface defect of this file.

I also saw that the private `normNat_lambda` restates the existing `normNat_lambdaE` in CubicGauss/Cutoffs.lean. That is duplication, not a simp-interface issue, so it is outside this rubric.

I could not run Lean, so I made no claims about simp behaviour.
